questions.q: What is the naming pattern this lesson recommends for a flow's label?
options: Purpose only, as short as possible
A random unique ID generated by Flow Builder
The name of the person who built the flow
Object – Trigger Context – Purpose (e.g., 'Case - Before Save - Priority and Routing')
questions.explain: Object + Trigger Context + Purpose lets anyone scanning the Flows list tell what a flow touches and when it fires without opening it.

questions.q: Why do element labels (not just the flow's own name) matter?
options: Specific element labels turn the canvas itself into documentation, readable without opening each element's configuration
Element labels have no effect on anything and are purely cosmetic
Flow Builder requires unique element labels or it won't save
Element labels determine the flow's execution order
questions.explain: A Decision labeled 'Check Case Severity' instead of 'Decision' lets someone understand the flow's logic by reading labels top to bottom.

questions.q: What should a flow's Description field capture, at minimum, according to this lesson?
options: Nothing — it's optional and rarely used
The business problem it solves, who asked for it or why it exists, and any non-obvious dependencies or edge cases
Only the Salesforce API version the flow was built on
A list of every element's technical configuration
questions.explain: The Description field should document intent and context — the one thing that survives even after the original builder is gone.

questions.q: Combined with the one-flow-per-object-per-context rule from the previous lesson, what extra benefit does consistent flow naming provide?
options: It automatically bulkifies the flow
It removes the need for a Description field entirely
It makes it obvious at a glance whether a new rule belongs in an existing flow or needs a genuinely new one
It prevents the flow from ever needing a new version
questions.explain: Naming by Object + Trigger Context makes matching flows to new requirements immediate — a new Case Before-Save rule clearly belongs with the existing 'Case - Before Save' flow.

questions.q: What is the real cost of leaving elements named 'Decision,' 'Decision 2,' and 'Get Records' in a production flow?
options: It triggers a governor limit error
It prevents the flow from being activated
It automatically deactivates the previous version
It increases every future maintainer's time spent figuring out what the flow does instead of reading it directly
questions.explain: Vague labels don't break anything technically, but they impose a real ongoing cost on anyone who later needs to understand or modify the flow.
